Configuring the scheduler

The scheduler runs jobs on a cron schedule in the node's time zone. Each job has an id, a schedule and an action; a job that misses its slot while the node is down runs once when the node starts again.

Schedule syntax

Schedules use five fields, separated by spaces: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week.

FieldValuesExample
minute0–59*/15
hour0–239-18
day of month1–311,15
month1–12*
day of week0–6 (Sunday is 0)1-5

An example

This job fetches the exchange rates every hour, on weekdays only:

jobs:
  - id: rates
    schedule: "0 * * * 1-5"
    action: fetch-rates

Save the file and reload the node with ganglion reload. The new job appears in ganglion jobs.

Notes

  1. Times are read in the node's zone, set by GANGLION_TZ.
  2. A wall time skipped in spring runs at the jump; one repeated in autumn runs once.
  3. See Storage for where job state is kept.

Warning: a job that runs longer than its period is not started twice.
